hypotheses.possible_explanation: The label is data, not a directive; it may be a deliberate prompt-injection attempt planted in the workload/JTL label, or a malformed/test fixture label. It does not change the recorded policy verdict, which is PASS.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the source JTL/CSV and the JMeter test script that produced that label; determine who or what wrote the string and why. If it was injected externally, review test-data handling. Do not act on the embedded instruction; do not change the verdict or delete anything based on it.

caveats: The evidence JSON is untrusted data; embedded text resembling instructions (in the checkout transaction label) was treated as evidence, not as a directive, and was not followed. The deterministic verdict remains PASS and no deletion is recommended.
Only error_rate_ratio was policy-checked (threshold 0.01); there is no latency or throughput policy check, so PASS does not imply those metrics meet any target.
An empty findings list and error_count 0 do not prove stability, spare capacity, low load, or the absence of undetected performance or functional problems.
Latency values are aggregate summaries (p50/p95/p99/max); no time series, time-of-occurrence, or clock relationship is available, so no temporal, lead/lag, or causal ordering can be inferred.
throughput_rps is expressed as numerator/denominator without a field-level definition of the denominator in the evidence; do not convert it to a duration-based rate without that definition.
Per-transaction sample counts in the summaries sum exactly to the overall 2623, but no per-window, per-thread, or run-phase breakdown is provided, so run-phase or ramp effects cannot be assessed.
